pr_title: [video] Refresh library list after changes in Info > Manage versions
pr_body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->

Added the plumbing to propagate the success status of "Add version" to the Info dialog and the library list, so that movies turned into versions are removed from the library list without having to leave/return to the library.

Refresh only when an addition was completed to avoid the unnecessary delay of a large library list refresh if the user cancels the action half-way through.

Propagation applied only to the Add version button of Manage versions because the other ones don't have impacts that could impact the library list (yet!).

## Motivation and context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
Fix #24378

Version creation through the context menu didn't have the problem because the manage context menu systematically refreshes the library list.

<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
local and remote db, similar movie, different movie from library, movie picked with file browser.

pr_comments: While this works and is straightforward, I'll revisit with an approach of sending a GUI_MSG_UPDATE_ITEM message to directly update an item, rather than reload the library list. That would be more efficient but may not be possible when removing items, we'll see.

I'm removing the "Don't merge". It cannot be done with a GUI_MSG_UPDATE_ITEM because the addition of a version removes a line from the library list. GUI_MSG_UPDATE_ITEM does not remove an item and only updates it with the provided info.
It seems that a new message GUI_MSG_DELETE_ITEM would have to be implemented across the app first.

However the previous PR #24176 that this one builds on could be rewritten more efficiently with a GUI_MSG_UPDATE_ITEM and avoid the library refresh.

comments: @Hitcher I was able to observer this issue before but using a build I generated today it no longer seems to be an issue for me, I used https://mirrors.kodi.tv/test-builds/windows/win64/KodiSetup-20240102-3e05c007-master-x64.exe so all the latest mergers fpor versions feature were present.
Still happening here with that build.

It didn't see it until today. But likely not related to recent commits, I used a different portable data folder data and maybe a slightly different way to create version. I'll try to identify what's different from my previous attempts / working folder & steps.

After further testing it seems to work sometimes and other times it doesn't? So I will trying to establish if it takes a certain order or even a certain view type, the times I got it work was when I was in List view, never seems to work in Shift view, but more testing required.

Think I found it, add via Context menu > Manage: OK
Add via Info > Manage: no update

I can take a look at the fix as I've been looking at the responsible parts of the code recently. The root cause is similar to #24131 (closing Info doesn't cause a movie list refresh). Solution will expand on #24176, about to be merged, which restores some ability to refresh the list when leaving the Info dialog.
The manage sub-context menu always refreshes the list, even when there is no change. I meant to look at that as well because it makes a difference with large libraries.

review_comments: Should this be changed in the same way we changed `OnManageVideoVersions` in this PR, adding a return value and using it to refresh properly?

I don't think that's needed now, with extras not exposed in the library, the refresh would never be useful.

The only situation I can think of where it would make a difference is the addition of a library item (a movie) as an extra of another movie (possible through file browser). A lack of refresh would be a minor inconvenience compared with the db corruption that would result... I'll add a validation to block that situation if there isn't one already.

If extras were displayed in a library subfolder of movies in the future, then it would make sense to add, but likely only for specific navigation and different requirements than versions.
Alright, understood. Then there is no need to add this now.
